mainTopic: Can a slave appoint a שליח for his release document, and what do רבי מאיר and רבנן argue about when a slave frees himself with money from others?
overview: The גמרא asks whether, according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a slave can appoint a שליח to receive his release document. It concludes that he can, because the words "לה" "לה" link the slave to a woman's גט. This seems to clash with רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who said כהנים must be God's agents, since a person cannot send an agent to do what he cannot do himself. The גמרא answers that a ישראל has no connection at all to קרבנות, while a slave does have a connection to גיטין: a ברייתא shows he can receive another slave's release document. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's argument between רבי מאיר and רבנן about a slave freeing himself with money from others. רבה, quoting רב ששת, says they argue about a gift given on the condition that the master has no rights to it. רבי אלעזר says everyone agrees such a condition fails, and puts the argument in a gift given "on condition that you go free with it." Finally, the גמרא begins to show that each side seems to contradict itself, using a ברייתא that comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Can a slave appoint an agent to receive his release document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, an עבד כנעני can appoint a שליח to receive his גט שחרור from his master. It gives a reason for each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, can a Canaanite slave appoint an agent to receive his release document from his master? Maybe yes: since he learns "לה" "לה" from a woman, the slave is like a woman. Or maybe no: a woman can receive her own גט, so she can also appoint an agent. But a slave cannot receive his own document, so he cannot appoint an agent either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question with two possible answers. Can a slave send an agent to collect his freedom document?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר learns the slave's document from a woman's גט through the shared word "לה", so the slave should follow all the woman's rules, including using a שליח. Side two: a woman's power to appoint a שליח comes from her own power to receive her גט. A slave cannot receive his own document, so he has no power to pass on to an agent.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew
An agent who acts on someone's behalf
His document (here: the slave's release document, גט שחרור)
The word "to her" that appears in both topics and links the slave's document to a woman's גט
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a slave can be freed with a document; רבי שמעון בן אלעזר already holds that he can. The question is only whether an agent can receive that document for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view, discussed earlier on the daf, that a slave goes free with a document learned from a woman's גט.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the link "לה" "לה" make the slave like a woman even for appointing a שליח, or does a slave's inability to receive his own document block an agent?

steps.title: The answer: the slave is like a woman
steps.stepSummary: The one who asked the question answers it himself. Because of the link "לה" "לה", the slave is like a woman and can appoint a שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: After asking the question, he went back and answered it: "לה" "לה" is learned from a woman, so the slave is like a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The asker answers his own question. The slave can appoint an agent, just like a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first side wins. The link to a woman's גט carries over the woman's rules about agents. It does not matter that the slave cannot receive the document himself.

keyTerms.meaning: After he asked the question
He went back and answered it himself

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a slave can appoint a שליח to receive his release document, even though he cannot receive it himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This conclusion becomes the basis for the challenge against רב הונא in the next steps.

phrases.english: After he asked the question, he went back and answered it:
"lah" "lah" is learned from a woman, so he is like a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 by choosing the first side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The slave is like a woman, so he can appoint a שליח to receive his document.

steps.title: רב הונא: כהנים are God's agents, not ours
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's rule that כהנים are שלוחי דרחמנא. His reason: a person cannot send an agent to do what he himself cannot do. This sets up a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: These priests are the agents of the Merciful One. For if you think they are our agents, is there anything we cannot do ourselves but our agents can do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב הונא's statement to set up the next move. It is about to show that this statement clashes with the slave ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular Jew may not do the עבודה in the בית המקדש. So רב הונא argues that he cannot send a כהן to do it for him. That means the כהנים must be acting as God's agents. Behind this is a general rule: you can only send an agent for something you yourself could do.

keyTerms.meaning: Priests (כהנים)
Agents of the Merciful One (God's agents)
It enters your mind / you might think
Our agents

steps.confusionAlert: The word "ואלא" ("but then") shows the גמרא is not just adding a new teaching. It is getting ready to say that רב הונא's statement now seems to have a problem.

phrases.english: But then, that which was said by
Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua:
These priests are agents of the Merciful One.
For if it enters your mind
that they are our agents,
is there anything
that we cannot do ourselves

phrases.notes: A regular Jew may not do the Temple service, so he can't send a כהן to do it for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings in an outside statement that seems to conflict with the conclusion of step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים are שלוחי דרחמנא, because a person cannot appoint an agent for something he himself cannot do.

steps.title: The slave case seems to disprove רב הונא's logic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's rule. The slave cannot receive his own document, yet we just ruled that he can appoint a שליח to receive it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there really nothing like that? But there is the slave: he cannot receive his own document, yet he can appoint an agent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's reasoning using the slave ruling from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא assumed that no one can send an agent to do something he cannot do himself. The slave is a clear example of exactly that: he cannot receive his own document, but his agent can. So רב הונא's proof that כהנים must be God's agents seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! (introduces a challenge from a known case)
The slave
Appoint / make (someone an agent)

phrases.english: And is there not?! But there is the slave,
who cannot receive his own document himself,
and yet he can appoint an agent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 3 set up, using the conclusion of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's reasoning that an agent cannot do what the sender cannot do.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: the slave cannot receive his own document, yet he can appoint a שליח to receive it, as ruled in step 2.

steps.title: A slave has some connection to bills of release
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. A ישראל has nothing to do with קרבנות at all, but a slave does have a connection to גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not correct. A ישראל has no connection at all to the laws of קרבנות. A slave does have a connection to bills of release.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 4. It shows that רב הונא's rule does not contradict our ruling about the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule only applies when a person has no connection at all to the act, like a ישראל and קרבנות. The slave is different. He cannot receive his own גט, but he is not completely cut off from the world of גיטין. So he can still appoint a שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not so; the גמרא is rejecting the comparison
Connected to, has a part in
The laws of offerings

steps.whyThisMatters: It narrows רב הונא's rule. You need only some connection to the area of law, not the ability to do this exact act yourself.

phrases.english: But that is not so.
Israelites are not connected
to the laws of offerings at all;
a slave is connected to bills of release.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between total lack of connection and partial connection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the slave cannot receive his own גט, רב הונא's rule should stop him from appointing a שליח.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא's rule applies only to someone with no connection at all to that area of law. A slave has a connection to גיטין, so he can appoint a שליח.

steps.title: Proof that a slave can receive another slave's bill
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that a slave can receive another slave's גט שחרור from that slave's master, but not from his own master.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: a slave may receive the bill of release of another slave from that other slave's master. He may not receive it from his own master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the claim in Step 5 that a slave is connected to גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave can act as a receiver of a גט for a different slave, so he does have a role in גיטין. He cannot receive one from his own master. Whatever a slave holds belongs to his master, so the document would never leave the master's possession.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
It seems correct that
His fellow, here meaning another slave

steps.whatToRemember: A slave's partial role in גיטין, receiving for another slave, is enough to let him appoint a שליח for his own גט.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
It seems that a slave
may receive the bill of release of his fellow slave
from the hand of his fellow's master,
but not from the hand of his own master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the answer in Step 5
steps.raayaObject: That a slave is connected to גיטין
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that a slave may receive another slave's גט שחרור from that slave's master

steps.title: Suggesting what רבי מאיר and רבנן argue about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words about money from others. It suggests that רבי מאיר holds a slave or wife cannot own anything apart from the master or husband, and that רבנן hold they can.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the slave may pay with money only if it comes from others. Shall we say this is their argument? רבי מאיר holds that a slave cannot acquire without his master, and a woman cannot acquire without her husband. רבנן hold that a slave can acquire without his master, and a woman can acquire without her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה. It offers a possible explanation for the argument between רבי מאיר and רבנן, which the next step will test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן allow a slave to free himself with money he holds, as long as others gave it to him. רבי מאיר does not. The גמרא suggests a simple reason. For רבי מאיר, anything a slave gets goes straight to his master, so the slave never owns it. For רבנן, a slave can own something on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that, only if
Shall we say this is what they argue about?
Acquisition, ownership
Without his master, apart from the master

steps.confusionAlert: "Money from others" does not mean other people pay the master. It means money that others gave to the slave, which the slave then uses to free himself.

phrases.english: Provided that the money is from others.
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words. רבנן said a slave can free himself with money he holds, as long as it came from others.

phrases.english: Shall we say they argue about this:
that Rabbi Meir holds:
a slave has no acquisition without his master,
and a woman has no acquisition without her husband.
And the Rabbis hold:
a slave has acquisition without his master,
and a woman has acquisition without her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the שליח discussion back to a new line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle lies behind the argument between רבי מאיר and רבנן about a slave freeing himself with money from others
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suggested: they argue whether a slave or wife can own property apart from the master or husband

steps.title: Everyone agrees; the case is a gift with a condition
steps.stepSummary: רבה, quoting רב ששת, says everyone agrees that a slave or wife cannot acquire on their own. The argument is about a gift of a מנה given on the condition that the master has no rights to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב ששת: everyone agrees that a slave cannot acquire without his master, and a woman cannot acquire without her husband. The case here is where someone gave the slave a מנה and said: on the condition that your master has no rights to it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה rejects the suggestion of Step 7. He puts the argument into a narrower, special case instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 made רבי מאיר and רבנן argue about a basic rule. רבה says there is no argument about that rule: a slave cannot own anything apart from his master. The only question is whether the giver can keep the master out by setting a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
What case are we dealing with here?
A sum of money, one hundred זוז
On the condition that
Rights, control

phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין קִנְיָן לְעֶבֶד בְּלֹא רַבּוֹ,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees a slave has no acquisition without his master,
and a woman has no acquisition without her husband.
And here, what are we dealing with?
Where another person gave him a maneh,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לְרַבָּךְ רְשׁוּת בּוֹ״.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי מאיר and רבנן argue about the basic ownership rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Everyone agrees that a slave cannot own anything apart from his master. The argument is only about a gift given with a condition.

steps.title: Does the giver's condition work?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds the condition does nothing, so the master gets the money. רבנן hold the condition works, so the slave owns it and can use it to free himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: when the giver said "acquire," the slave acquired it and his master acquired it right away. When he added "on the condition," his words meant nothing. רבנן hold: since he said "on the condition," his condition works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each side views the case of a gift with a condition. This finishes רבה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the master gets the money the moment the slave does, so the condition cannot stop it. The slave never owns money to pay for his freedom. For רבנן, the condition keeps the master out, so the slave truly owns the money and can free himself with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquire! (said when giving something)
He said nothing; his words have no effect
His condition works

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, the argument between רבי מאיר and רבנן is only whether a giver's condition can keep the master from getting a gift to the slave. Everyone agrees that, normally, what a slave acquires goes to his master.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
when he said to him "acquire,"
the slave acquires and his master acquires.
phrases.notes: It happens at the same moment: the instant the slave gets it, it passes to his master.

phrases.english: And when he said to him "on the condition,"
he has said nothing to him.
And the Rabbis hold:
since he said to him "on the condition,"
his condition is effective.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: כִּי אָמַר לֵיהּ ״קְנִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two opinions within the case set up in Step 8
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר: the condition does not work, so the master gets the money. רבנן: the condition works, so the slave can free himself with that money.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: A different case for the argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says everyone agrees a slave acquires and his master automatically acquires through him. The argument is about a gift given 'on condition that you go free with it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: In a case like this, everyone agrees that the slave acquires the money and his master acquires it from him. So what case are we talking about? Someone else gave the slave a מנה and said, 'on condition that you go free with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר offers a new way to explain the argument in the משנה, different from רבה's way in Step 8. He says that in רבה's case, where the giver said 'your master has no rights to it,' everyone agrees the money still goes to the master. So he moves the argument to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבה and רבי אלעזר agree that whatever a slave acquires goes to his master. The difference is that רבה thought a condition like 'your master has no rights to it' could be argued about. רבי אלעזר holds that everyone agrees such a condition cannot keep the master out. So the argument must be about a different condition: 'go free with it.'

keyTerms.meaning: In any case like this
Everyone agrees
The slave acquires, and his master acquires through him
What case are we dealing with?
A sum of one hundred זוז
On condition that

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רבה's case. רבה's giver said 'the master has no rights to it.' רבי אלעזר's giver said 'go free with it.'

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
In any case like this,

phrases.english: everyone agrees
that the slave acquires, and his master acquires

Such as where another person gave him a מנה

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁתֵּצֵא בּוֹ לְחֵירוּת״.
phrases.english: and said to him: "On condition that you go out to freedom with it."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: כֹּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation of the argument, in place of רבה's explanation from Steps 8 and 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees a slave acquires and his master acquires through him. The argument is about a gift given 'on condition that you go free with it.'

steps.title: How each side reads the 'go free with it' condition
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the slave got the money and the master took it, so the condition means nothing. רבנן say the giver never gave the money to the slave for himself, so it frees him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: once the giver said 'acquire,' the slave acquired and his master acquired. When he added 'on condition,' he said nothing at all. רבנן hold: the giver did not give the money to the slave for himself either, because all he said was 'on condition that you go free with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each side's reasoning under רבי אלעזר's version of the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the word 'acquire' already gave the money to the slave, and so to the master. The condition comes too late to change that. For רבנן, the giver only gave the money for one purpose, buying freedom. The slave never owned it as his own, so the master has nothing to take, and the money goes toward the slave's freedom.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquire! (the word used to hand over ownership)
He said nothing (his words have no effect)
To him himself
Gives ownership
Freedom

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר: רבי מאיר says the money goes to the master. רבנן say the money was never the slave's to lose, so it frees him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
when he said to him "Acquire,"

"On condition that you go out to freedom with it."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: כִּי אֲמַר לֵיהּ ״קְנִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning of each side under the case רבי אלעזר set up in Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר: the condition does nothing, so the master gets the money. רבנן: the money was given only for freedom, so it frees the slave.

steps.title: Setting up contradictions within רבי מאיר and within רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces it will point out a contradiction between two statements of רבי מאיר, and between two statements of רבנן, from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא points out a contradiction between one ruling of רבי מאיר and another ruling of רבי מאיר, and between one ruling of רבנן and another ruling of רבנן. As it was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to quote a ברייתא that seems to clash with what each side said in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is not one side against the other. Each side seems to contradict itself. The ברייתא that shows this comes right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: He pointed out a contradiction (literally, 'he threw' one source against another)

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא (quoted next) seems to show each side ruling the opposite way elsewhere.
